patterns.usage_note: まで marks the far end of a continuous stretch — of space, of time, or of degree — and implies the whole span leading up to it, which is why the predicate is usually durative (待つ, 歩く, 続ける). Keep it apart from までに, which sets a deadline by which a one-shot event must happen: 五時まで待つ is waiting the whole time, 五時までに来る is arriving at some point before five. In real Japanese まで also attaches to a plain-form verb (終わるまで待つ) and pairs with から for an explicit start point; the corpus rule recorded here covers only the noun-attached use.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]は夕方[ゆうがた]まで図書館[としょかん]で調[しら]べ物[もの]をする。
examples.english: I'll be doing research at the library until early evening today.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]までなら歩[ある]いて十分[じゅっぷん]もかからない。
examples.english: As far as the station it's not even a ten-minute walk.

examples.ruby: 荷物[にもつ]は玄関[げんかん]まで運[はこ]んでおきました。
examples.english: I've carried the bags as far as the entryway for you.
